content: Nothing can be undone, and nothing can be wiped out. Having been is also a kind of being, perhaps the most secure kind of being.
author: Viktor Frankl
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

In Viktor Frankl's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
